reasons: **Heat is the main limit.** Even the hottest-running workers should stay just under the safe body temperature (38.0 °C). The closest call is less than a tenth of a degree from the limit, so watch for signs of overheating and enforce breaks.
**Marcus is protected.** As a new hire whose body hasn't adjusted to the heat yet, he isn't given the hardest physical jobs during the hottest parts of the day. Others pick up that load.

**Other options get the same work done but run hotter.** We'd finish about 90% of the most important work either way. This plan is the safest of the three.

Hard safety rules:
- Every worker's 90th percentile core temperature must stay below 38.0 °C all shift. Harder work, sun and high WBGT heat people up; 30-min shade rests cool them down.
- Breaks: at most 3 work slots in a row, then a 'rest' slot; at most 2 in a row if any of those slots has WBGT >= 30.0 °C.
- No outdoor tasks during hazards that stop outdoor work. After lightning, outdoor work stays stopped for 30 more minutes.
- Workers who are not acclimatized never do very_heavy tasks when WBGT >= 28.0 °C.
Validity: one entry per slot per worker; off-site workers rest; skills and allowed slots must match.
